transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Jon Ramos (Redwood SE), Zoe Park (Redwood SE), Evelyn Park (Polaris Head of Platform), Miguel Santos (Polaris DevOps), Hannah Lee (Polaris Security), Samir Khan (Polaris Product)

Auto-generated Summary (optional):
Quick orientation to Redwood onboarding runbook, alignment on pilot success criteria (latency, cost, quality), network/VPC checklist review, and schedule next technical deep-dive. Action items and SOC2/security artifacts to be shared.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Monroe: All right good afternoon everyone, um thanks for carving time on valentines day i guess for infra talks, appreciate it. i'm alex from redwood, i'm the account lead. quick round robin, can folks say name and role?
[00:08] Evelyn Park: Evelyn Park, head of platform at Polaris.
[00:11] Miguel Santos: Miguel, DevOps manager.
[00:13] Hannah Lee: Hannah, security lead.
[00:15] Samir Khan: Samir, product.
[00:18] Priya Desai: Priya, your CSM, i'll run the onboarding beats.
[00:21] Jon Ramos: Jon, SE, i'll be doing the technical deep-dive and benchwork.
[00:24] Zoe Park: Zoe, solutions eng, i'll join the VPC and private deploy conversation.
[00:27] Alex Monroe: Cool. Agenda — quick intro + success criteria, runbook walkthrough, network & infra Qs, security/compliance questions, next steps. Sound good?
[00:35] Evelyn Park: Yep that matches our expectations. we're particularly keen on latency targets and making sure we can keep cost predictable for the pilot.
[00:41] Alex Monroe: Perfect, that's one of our main focuses. Priya i'll hand it to you to go over the runbook and timeline.
[00:46] Priya Desai: Thanks. So the onboarding runbook — we'll send a link after the call but the bones are: week 0 is access and infra checks, week 1 we deploy a staging tenant and run basic inference smoke tests, week 2 we run workload simulation + perf bench, week 3 is tuning and SLO alignment then pilot. For pilot success we typically ask for three criteria: functional correctness from your eval sets, latency SLOs at 95th percentile, and monthly cost within agreed budget.
[01:12] Samir Khan: On the functional correctness side we'll bring our prompt set and expected outputs. is there a place to upload that?
[01:17] Priya Desai: Yep we'll provision a shared folder and you can drop prompts, also link you to the eval framework.
[01:21] Miguel Santos: Quick question on network: do you require inbound peering or do we outbound to you? we need to understand egress flow, firewall rules, and MTU requirements (we hit weird fragmentation on some clusters).
[01:32] Jon Ramos: Great question. For Redwood hosted API it's outbound from your VPC to our public endpoints; for Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) we support VPC peering and S2S VPN. MTUwise generally standard 1500 works, but we have seen 9000 jumbo frames depending on infra; the primary thing is to ensure no path MTU blackhole and allow for long-lived websocket streams on 443 if you use streaming responses.
[01:54] Miguel Santos: And for private deployment do you do peering or transit gateways?
[01:58] Zoe Park: We support both depending on cloud provider — for AWS we can do VPC peering or Transit Gateway; for GCP we use VPC peering in most setups. We'll send a network checklist with CIDR ranges and ip lists you need to whitelist.
[02:12] Hannah Lee: From security we need SOC 2 type ii, iso certs, and pen test history. also interested in key management — do you integrate with customer managed KMS or HSM?
[02:22] Priya Desai: Yes we have SOC 2 and ISO documents, we'll attach them. For key management — for Redwood hosted we offer BYOK with cloud KMS integrations; for Private/on-prem we can integrate with customer HSM/KMS via KMIP or cloud KMS depending on the environment.
[02:36] Hannah Lee: Also data retention and audit logs — we need immutable audit logs for at least 1 year, and log separation so we don't see raw customer tokens in application logs.
[02:45] Jon Ramos: Our default logging keeps token-level redaction, and the console provides per-request tracing; audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM via syslog or S3 exports depending on the deployment. We'll include a sample retention policy.
[02:57] Evelyn Park: On latency — our bar for the feature is 95th p95 under 200ms for typical prompts ~256 tokens, but for longer inference we can accept higher. can you get us a sense of what model/instance types you'd recommend?
[03:10] Jon Ramos: For that profile, on hosted we'd recommend a mid-sized quantized model on a T4-equivalent GPU or the Redwood-optimized instance family; for Dedicated we'd look at A10/RTX-class depending on concurrency. That said, latency is sensitive to sequence length and batch configuration. we also have prefix KV caching and batching knobs to stay under SLO.
[03:33] Samir Khan: You mentioned KV cash earlier in docs — is that the same as KV cache? docs had a typo.
[03:37] Zoe Park: Yeah that's a docs typo, it's KV cache. Apologies — we'll fix that string.
[03:41] Miguel Santos: Cost question — can you provide example cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated reserved capacity?
[03:48] Alex Monroe: We'll provide ranges. Hosted is straightforward per-token pricing; Dedicated is commit + utilization model which can significantly lower per-token cost if you have steady qps. We'll send an estimate spreadsheet after this call.
[03:58] Hannah Lee: For compliance, do you conduct regular pen tests and third-party audits? we need findings summaries, remediation timelines.
[04:05] Priya Desai: Yes, we can share our last 12 months of audit summaries and pen test cover letters. If additional attestation is required for your vendor risk team we'll coordinate with security to provide redacted reports.
[04:15] Evelyn Park: Integration-wise we'll want staging->canary->prod rollout. what's the typical timeline from staging to pilot traffic?
[04:22] Priya Desai: Typical is 2–4 weeks depending on bench results and integration effort. We'll propose an initial pilot of 4 weeks to gather metrics.
[04:30] Jon Ramos: On the bench side, we'll ask you to provide a traffic trace or representative qps/seq length distribution. we run local perf with the same model variants and produce a report with tokens/sec, p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:45] Miguel Santos: We can export traces from our test harness, i'll add that to the action items.
[04:49] Samir Khan: On the product side we also need structured output support — we rely on function-like responses, schema enforcement. does the runtime support structured outputs and function calling?
[04:58] Zoe Park: Yes, streaming + function-tool-calling style outputs are supported. We also have structured output validators and will help set up guardrails in the eval harness.
[05:07] Hannah Lee: For RBAC and SSO — we use SAML via Okta. can we federate to the Redwood console and provision teams?
[05:14] Priya Desai: Yes, SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning is supported. We'll share the SSO setup doc and a step-by-step.
[05:21] Evelyn Park: Any known limitations for on-prem air-gapped?
[05:24] Jon Ramos: Air-gapped is possible but requires the on-prem package and a slightly longer lead time for deployment — packaging, hardware validation, and KMS/HSM integration usually add 3–6 weeks depending on site access.
[05:36] Miguel Santos: For the pilot, we'd probably start hosted to move fast, and if performance/privacy needs dictate, transition to Dedicated or Private.
[05:43] Alex Monroe: Exactly that phased approach is common — hosted for rapid validation, then Dedicated reserve for cost predictability, Private for strict residency or air-gap.
[05:51] Priya Desai: Ok next practical steps: i'll share runbook and SOC2/ISO docs by friday. Jon and Zoe will schedule a 60m VPC deep-dive with Miguel for next week. Alex will send pilot pricing spreadsheet. Evelyn/Polaris to confirm pilot models and representative traffic.
[06:06] Evelyn Park: Sounds good. quick note for your pricing spreadsheet include a 'break-glass' option for short bursts (we need occasional spiky traffic).
[06:13] Alex Monroe: We'll add burst capacity options and example overage behavior.
[06:16] Hannah Lee: Can we get a copy of your data processing addendum and subprocessor list?
[06:20] Priya Desai: Yes, will include those docs.
[06:23] Alex Monroe: Any other Qs?
[06:25] Samir Khan: one more — do you have a sandbox model we can try without sending PHI? small sample env?
[06:30] Priya Desai: We'll provision a sandbox tenant that uses synthetic data, you can test end-to-end without sending sensitive data.
[06:35] Miguel Santos: ok good.
[06:37] Alex Monroe: cool — recap of action items and owners we'll email in 30 mins, and priya will attach links. thanks everyone, talk soon.
[06:44] Meeting ends.

Notes: slight transcription glitches present (speaker tags sometimes generic). Links referenced: https://redwood.example.com/onboard-runbook, https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 (placeholders)
